title: Commit smoothing and overcommit experiments
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet captures experiment notes, assumptions, and column layouts for a commit smoothing + controlled overcommit pricing simulator intended to inform Dedicated capacity SKU design. Goal is to quantify realistic utilization uplift achievable without violating SLO-backed latency or creating risky tail failure modes, and to produce recommended pricing bands and guardrails.

Executive summary (short):
- Hypothesis: modest, policy-driven overcommit (10–30% average over a long horizon, with short-term burst controls) substantially reduces unit cost while keeping customer-facing SLOs intact for most workloads.
- Approach: Build a stochastic simulator driven by historical per-customer throughput traces (seq length distribution, qps patterns, burst windows) and GPU pool sizing constraints. Apply several smoothing policies (EWMA smoothing, weekly commit bucketing, auction-based burst credits) and measure utilization, blocking rate, and latency-impact probability.
- Early finding: A 15% nominal overcommit with a 95th-percentile burst headroom policy reduced price-per-token by ~9% in our synthetic mixes and introduced <1.8% probability of 99.9th percentile latency >baseline for latency-sensitive profiles.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline GPU amortization cost = $X per GPU per month (placeholder to be replaced by finance inputs).
- Workload mix split: latency-sensitive (22%), throughput-batch (38%), embeddings-heavy (40%).
- Sequence length distribution derived from hosted API logs sampled over 90 days.
- Job preemption: non-critical background inference can be preempted to free KV cache; critical routes are pinned to guaranteed pool slices.
- Burst definition: any 5-minute window exceeding 2x rolling 1-hour median QPS counts as a burst.

Simulation schema (columns and sample formulas):
- col:customer_id (string)
- col:commit_tier (string) -> tiers: small, standard, enterprise
- col:committed_gpus (int)
- col:observed_qps_trace (list-of-numeric-tokens-per-interval)  -- in sheet represented as encoded CSV string
- col:ewma_lambda (float) -- smoothing parameter used for smoothing policy
- col:smoothed_commit (float) -- computed EWMA of recent usage
- col:overcommit_ratio (float) -- policy set; e.g. 1.15 means 15% overcommit allowed
- col:burst_credit_balance (float) -- credits available to customer for bursts
- col:allocated_effective_gpus (float) -- committed_gpus * overcommit_ratio adjusted by smoothing/guardrails
- col:utilization_percent (float) -- observed_tokens / (allocated_effective_gpus * capacity_per_gpu)
- col:block_events_count (int) -- number of times requests were rejected/queued beyond threshold
- col:latency_tail_violation_prob (float) -- estimator of probability that 99.9th latency > SLA
- col:unit_cost_estimate (float) -- amortized cost / effective_tokens_served
- col:recommended_price_adjustment (float) -- suggested % change to list price for tier
- col:notes (string)

Key policies to test (distinct):
1) EWMA smoothing + conservative headroom: smoothed commit = EWMA(usage), allow overcommit = min(1.15, 1 + 0.25*(smoothed_commit/committed)), enforce pool-level headroom floor.
2) Sliding-week bucket commits: customers choose weekly commit buckets; overcommit allowed only for daily bursts and reconciled monthly with penalty credits.
3) Auctioned burst credits: sell burst credits at low friction; credits consumed during 5-minute bursts; credits refill monthly. Simulate both free initial credit and paid models.
4) Priority pinning hybrid: critical endpoints can pin a % of a GPU pool (no overcommit); remaining capacity subject to aggressive overcommit.
5) Stochastic trimmed overcommit: allow aggressive overcommit (up to 2x) but only for low-percentile workloads and with automatic downgrade to spot-model if sustained.

Metrics to capture (sheet tabs):
- Summary by policy: avg_utilization, cost_per_effective_token, 95th_latency_increase, blocking_rate, monthly_revenue_delta.
- Tail risk matrix: for each policy, show probability mass over latencies (p(latency_increase > X)).
- Customer-level impact: delta unit cost, recommended new tier or credit requirement per customer.
- Pool-level safety: headroom usage across simulated days, worst-day saturation events, time-to-degrade.

Sensitivity knobs to expose to product/finance:
- Overcommit cap (0–100%)
- Burst window length (1m, 5m, 15m)
- Credit refill cadence (daily/weekly/monthly)
- Fine-grained ability to pin k% of pool to SLA classes
- Price for burst credit (if monetizing)
- Penalty recovery rate for sustained overuse (reduce overcommit allowance)

Illustrative scenario (textual walkthrough):
- Customer A: committed 4 GPUs, pattern is steady with occasional 10m bursts. EWMA smoothing with overcommit 1.15 results in effective allocation 4.6 GPUs. Over 30 days, average utilization rises from 65% -> 78%. Blocking events reduced to zero, cost per effective token falls by ~11%. Worst-day shows a 2% chance of tail latency > baseline threshold, mitigated by temporary borrowing of neighbor pool in the simulation (policy: cross-pool loan within same latency tier).

Risks and failure modes (and mitigations):
- Risk: systemic burst correlation across many customers causing pool-wide saturation. Mitigation: implement pool-level shortfall alarms, auto-failover to lower-cost model variants, and a global emergency circuit breaker that disables overcommit for N minutes.
- Risk: gaming the smoothing window (customers shifting load to exploit credits). Mitigation: anomaly detection, smoothing windows with random jitter, and tiered penalties for anomalous patterns.
- Risk: KV cache thrash when preempting long-lived sessions. Mitigation: only preempt batch/embeddings endpoints; require warm-start eligibility checks.

Recommendations (actionable):
- Build a first-pass simulator tab that accepts per-customer synthetic traces (CSV) and runs the five policies above. Add a summary dashboard tab with the metrics listed.
- For initial product experiment, trial policy 1 (EWMA + conservative headroom) with a 10–20% overcommit cap and optional burst credits for Standard and Enterprise tiers.
- For pricing: present two SKUs for Dedicated: "Committed" (no overcommit, higher $/GPU) and "Committed+" (supports smoothing/overcommit, ~8–12% lower $/GPU but with credits and rules).
- Instrument and run A/B with a subset of low-correlation customers for 30 days before wider rollout. Capture real tail-latency telemetry and re-run sensitivity.

Next steps / TODOs (who/when):
- Samir: wire up synthetic trace generator and seed with 90-day host logs (by 2024-12-01).
- Priya: model finance amortization inputs and provide GPU cost baselines (by 2024-11-20).
- Ava: implement sheet tabs and sanity-check formulas, create visualization for tail risk (by 2024-12-10).
- Backend: export 30-day anonymized traces for 100 customers across tiers (request ticket JIRA-INF-1423).

Appendix: quick formulas and heuristics for the sheet (paste-friendly):
- EWMA: S_t = lambda*X_t + (1-lambda)*S_{t-1}
- effective_alloc = committed_gpus * min(overcommit_cap, 1 + alpha * (smoothed_commit/committed - 1))
- utilization = observed_tokens / (effective_alloc * tokens_per_gpu_per_period)
- unit_cost_estimate = (gpu_hour_amortization * allocated_gpu_hours) / total_tokens_served
- burst_credit_charge = max(0, (burst_minutes_used - free_credit_minutes)) * price_per_minute_credit

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc intentionally heavy on formulas and experiments. The sheet tab names should be: inputs, per-customer-traces, scenario-simulator, summary-dashboard, tail-risk, sensitivity-grid, customer-recs.
- I intentionally encoded traces as CSV strings in the per-customer tab for early experiments to avoid building a heavy importer. We should replace with proper time-series columns once the simulator is stabilized.
- Please flag any missing guardrails that would create unacceptable business risk (e.g., single-tenant peak storms, regulatory constraints for private deployments).

End of doc.
